gaps.text: In-line measurement of Medium optical clarity / turbidity and excipient background with turbidity or optical-density check during method development
In-line measurement of Medium temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: UV-Vis and Raman probes must sample the same vessel region and their data synchronised to a common time step. Start with one model per method, then fuse (e.g. concatenated, block-scaled spectra) and validate against HPLC on held-out runs. The fused model must beat the best single method, otherwise drop the second instrument.)
Dissolution testing itself, USP apparatus geometry, and fiber-optic dissolution systems are not covered by the supplied material.

items.finding: In a study comparing UV and Raman spectroscopy for in-line monitoring, data fusion techniques did not improve prediction accuracy above the prediction accuracy of the UV-based PLS model.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests that combining sensors may not always outperform a single well-performing sensor like UV-Vis, so rigorous validation against reference methods is essential to justify the added complexity.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study investigated monoclonal antibody downstream processing rather than dissolution testing, so matrix effects and process dynamics differ significantly.

citation.quote: Furthermore, data fusion strategies were investigated by combining both sensors in hierarchical PLS models or in CNNs. Among the tested options, UV spectroscopy alone allowed for the most precise and accurate prediction of the mAb concentration.
